change.describe: branch `pr-90939-flat` of grafana-90939-flat against cca9dee702ac4338ddc38aa56257273b8143e32e (merge-base cca9dee)
change.title: pr-90939-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so cold-start requests each re-read the manifest one after another
findings.body:
When the cache is empty, each concurrent caller passes the RLock check at lines 41-47, then waits on `Lock()` at line 48. Once the first caller has filled `entryPointAssetsCache`, every queued caller still runs `readWebAssetsFromFile` at line 60 again, one at a time. On startup, a burst of `/` (index.go:82), `/api/frontend/settings` (frontendsettings.go:62) and recovery (recovery.go:141) requests therefore parses `assets-manifest.json` once per request, in sequence. The old code also did this, but in parallel.

The same applies when the manifest is missing or invalid. `result` is nil, line 69 stores nil, and from then on every request goes through the exclusive lock and fails one at a time. Before this change those requests failed concurrently.

A double-checked lock fixes this. After `Lock()`, add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. In Dev mode the cache is skipped on purpose, so the re-read there is expected.

findings.title: No test exercises the new locking in GetWebAssets
findings.body: webassets_test.go only tests `readWebAssetsFromFile`, and the CDN test is skipped. Nothing calls `GetWebAssets` at all, so `go test -race` cannot catch a regression of the data race this change fixes. A small test would cover it: point `cfg.StaticRootPath` at a temp directory holding `build/assets-manifest.json` copied from testdata, then call `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines.

contracts.action: GetWebAssets now reads the package-level cache under an RWMutex read lock and fills it under the write lock
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: unsynchronized read/write of entryPointAssetsCache. Callers: pkg/api/index.go:82, pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62, pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141
contracts.before_after: Callers only read the returned *EntryPointAssets (index.go builds IndexViewData; frontendsettings.go hashes the fields at lines 63-71; recovery.go:142-143 substitutes an empty DTO on nil). None of them mutate the shared pointer. SetContentDeliveryURL is called only on the freshly read result, before it is stored (line 64). So sharing the cached pointer without a lock after it is returned is safe.
contracts.visible_effect: Index HTML, frontend settings hash and the panic error page get the same asset list as before. The data race on the global is gone.
contracts.failure_mode: On a read error, result is nil and line 69 stores nil. The error goes back to index.go:83-85 (request fails) and frontendsettings.go:63 (assets hash is skipped); recovery.go ignores it. Later calls retry, now one at a time under the write lock. A panic inside the locked section unlocks through the deferred Unlock at line 49, so the recovery middleware calling GetWebAssets again cannot deadlock.

summary: The change puts a sync.RWMutex around the global `entryPointAssetsCache` in GetWebAssets, which removes a data race. All three callers (index.go, frontendsettings.go, recovery.go) only read the returned DTO, so sharing the cached pointer is safe. Nothing blocks the merge. Two optional suggestions: re-check the cache after taking the write lock, so cold-start requests (and every request while the manifest is missing) don't re-read the manifest one at a time; and add a concurrent test so the race detector covers GetWebAssets. The PR body ("Frontend Asset Optimization") doesn't describe what the change actually does, which is a concurrency fix.
